title: Logarithmic-space recognition of valid encodings
statement: Let $L$ consist of the Boolean words of the form $[?]$; more precisely, words that encode a pair whose first component is a string of $n$ ones for some $n\in\mathbb N$, and whose second component is a canonical Boolean word (empty or ending in $1$), using the encoding that doubles each bit of the first component and then appends $01$ and the second component. Then $L$ belongs to nondeterministic logarithmic space: there is a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with a fixed finite number of work tapes and a constant $c\in\mathbb N$ that halts on every input along every choice sequence of a common length for that input, uses at most $c(\lfloor\log_2 |x|\rfloor+1)$ work-tape cells on each such sequence, and accepts exactly the words in $L$.
